bands.1:
"Maxx it out, Vantafam!"

The voice blasts out of the cracked tablet. Everyone on the boat groans.

On the screen, Maxx Vantablack zooms across the sea on a gold jet ski. His silver hair sticks up like a wave. His teeth are so white they sparkle. He has forty million followers. They call themselves the Vantafam.

"Today I am rescuing a poor little Creature!" Maxx shouts.

A tiny Creature is stuck in a net. Maxx pulls it free and cries big, shiny tears.

"Smash that heart button like it owes you money!" he sobs.

Millions of hearts fill the screen.

You are the captain of a small, leaky boat called the Soggy Biscuit. Your crew is squashed around the tablet with you. Tully counts everything. Gus loves gross science. Zed loves games. Indi draws. Mo cooks, badly.

"Pause it," says Wren. Wren looks after hurt animals. She zooms in on the net. A tiny gold logo is stitched into it. Two Xs.

"That's his own net," Wren says. "He set the trap himself."

Gus bangs the table so hard that his slime jar burps.

Wren unrolls an old map. Eight Islands have gold crosses on them. "Maxx has a secret base on each one," she says.

"Where did you get this?" Tully asks.

"Found it," says Wren. She does not look up.

Mo puts down a bowl of fish-finger custard. "Why did the Creature swim away?" he asks. "It didn't want to be Maxx-imum content!"

Everyone groans again. Then they all look at you.

"Your call, Captain," says Zed.

"We break them out," you say. "Every one. And we get proof."

The tablet buzzes. Maxx is live again. He holds up a photo. It is the Soggy Biscuit.

"See you soon, Captain," he says.

The screen goes black.
bands.2:
"Maxx it out, Vantafam!"

The voice blasts out of the cracked tablet, and everyone on the boat groans at once.

On the screen, Maxx Vantablack carves across the sea on his gold jet ski. His silver hair is sprayed into a perfect wave. His teeth are so white that his viewers wear sunnies. He has forty million followers, and they call themselves the Vantafam.

"Today, fam, I'm rescuing a poor little Creature!" Maxx shouts.

A tiny Creature is tangled in a net, shaking with fear. Maxx lifts it free and squeezes out one fat, glittering tear.

"Smash that heart button like it owes you money!" he sobs.

Millions of hearts flood the screen.

You are the captain of the Soggy Biscuit, a small boat that leaks whenever anyone sneezes. Your crew is squashed around the tablet with you.

"Pause it," says Wren, the crew's animal rescuer. She zooms in on the net. Stitched into the rope is a tiny gold logo: two Xs.

"That's his own net," Wren says quietly. "He set the trap himself."

For a moment, nobody speaks. Then Gus slams the table so hard that his jar of homemade slime burps.

Wren unrolls a crumpled map of the archipelago. Eight Islands are marked with gold crosses. "Maxx has a secret base on every one," she says. "That's where he keeps the Creatures he catches."

"Where did you get this?" asks Tully, narrowing her eyes.

"Found it," says Wren. She doesn't look up.

Indi is already drawing a moustache on a poster of Maxx. Zed cracks his knuckles. "Eight bases," he says. "That's eight boss levels."

Mo slides a bowl of fish-finger custard onto the table. "Why did the Creature swim away from Maxx?" he asks. "It didn't want to be Maxx-imum content!"

Everyone groans again, louder this time. Then, one by one, they turn to look at you.

"Your call, Captain," says Zed.

You look at the map, then at the frightened Creature frozen on the screen. "We break them out," you say. "Every single one. And we collect proof that he's lying."

The tablet buzzes. Maxx is live again.

"Oh, one more thing, Vantafam," he purrs. "I hear a little crew out there thinks I'm a fake."

He holds up a photo. It's the Soggy Biscuit.

"See you soon, Captain."

The screen goes black.

The voice blasts out of the cracked tablet, and everyone aboard the Soggy Biscuit groans at exactly the same time.

On the screen, Maxx Vantablack carves across the sea on his gold jet ski, the Gold Rush. Behind him floats his mega-yacht, the Vantadome, which has a glass dome on top and a waterslide off the back. A tiny Creature is tangled in a net, trembling as the waves slap it about. Maxx lifts it out tenderly and squeezes out one fat, glittering tear.

"Smash that heart button like it owes you money!" he sobs.

Millions of hearts flood the screen. Wren flinches, as if the words have stung her.

For a long moment, nobody speaks. Then Gus slams the table so hard that his jar of homemade slime burps a green bubble.

Wren unrolls a crumpled map of the archipelago. Eight Islands are marked with gold crosses. "Maxx has a secret base on every one of them," she says. "That's where he keeps the Creatures he catches."

"Found it," says Wren. She doesn't look up.

"I like those odds," says Gus. "Four is more than none."

Mo slides a bowl of fish-finger custard onto the table. It wobbles in a way that custard shouldn't. "Why did the Creature swim away from Maxx?" he asks. "It didn't want to be Maxx-imum content!"

"Oh, one more thing, Vantafam," he purrs. "I hear there's a little crew out there who thinks I'm a fake."

He holds up a photo. It's the Soggy Biscuit, leak and all.

"See you soon, Captain."

The screen goes black.
bands.4:
"Maxx it out, Vantafam!"

The voice blasts out of the cracked tablet, and everyone aboard the Soggy Biscuit groans in perfect, miserable harmony.

On the screen, Maxx Vantablack carves across the turquoise sea on his gold jet ski, the Gold Rush, spraying rainbows of mist behind him. In the distance floats his mega-yacht, the Vantadome, which has a glittering glass dome on top and a corkscrew waterslide off the back. His silver hair is sprayed into a wave so perfect that it doesn't move in the wind. His teeth are so blindingly white that a warning flashes up telling viewers to put on their sunnies. He has forty million followers, and they call themselves the Vantafam.

"Today, fam, I'm rescuing a poor, helpless little Creature!" Maxx announces, pressing a hand to his heart.

A tiny Creature is tangled in a net, trembling as the waves slap it about. Maxx scoops it out with exaggerated tenderness and squeezes out one fat, glittering tear that rolls down his cheek in slow motion.

"Smash that heart button like it owes you money!" he sobs.

Millions of hearts flood the screen. Beside you, Wren flinches, as if the catchphrase has stung her.

You are the captain of the Soggy Biscuit, a small, stubborn boat that springs a fresh leak whenever anyone sneezes. Your crew is squashed around the tablet with you, knees knocking and elbows everywhere.

"Pause it," says Wren, the crew's animal rescuer. She zooms in on the net until the picture goes blurry, then sharp again. Stitched into the rope is a tiny gold logo: two Xs.

"That's his own net," Wren says quietly. "He set the trap himself."

For a long moment, the only sound is the slosh of water in the bilge. Then Gus slams the table so hard that his jar of homemade slime burps a green bubble onto the ceiling.

Wren unrolls a crumpled, salt-stained map of the archipelago. Eight Islands are marked with gold crosses. "Maxx has a secret base on every one of them," she says. "That's where he keeps the Creatures he catches, until he needs them for a video."

"Where exactly did you get this?" asks Tully, narrowing her eyes.

"Found it," says Wren. She keeps her eyes on the map.

Indi is already drawing an enormous curly moustache on a poster of Maxx, adding a monobrow for good measure. Zed cracks his knuckles. "Eight bases," he says. "That's eight boss levels, and we haven't even unlocked a save point."

"Statistically," says Tully, "a crew this small has a four per cent chance of beating someone that famous. The Reef Rays had better odds last season, and they lost every single game."

"I like those odds," says Gus. "Four is more than none. That's not maths, that's science."

Mo slides a bowl of fish-finger custard onto the table. It wobbles in a way that custard should never wobble, and one fish finger slowly sinks like a shipwreck. "Why did the Creature swim away from Maxx?" he asks, grinning. "It didn't want to be Maxx-imum content!"

Everyone groans again, louder this time. Then, one by one, they turn to look at you.

"Your call, Captain," says Zed.

You look at the map, with its eight gold crosses, and then at the frightened Creature frozen on the screen. "We break them out," you say. "Every single one. And we collect so much proof that the whole Vantafam finally sees what he's really doing."

Nobody cheers, exactly, but Mo quietly pushes the custard away, which is almost the same thing.

The tablet buzzes. Maxx is live again, and this time his famous smile has gone thin and sharp.

"Oh, one more thing, Vantafam," he purrs, leaning so close to the camera that his nostrils fill the screen. "I hear there's a little crew out there who thinks I'm a fake."

He holds up a photo. It's the Soggy Biscuit, leak, slime stain and all.

"See you soon, Captain."

The screen goes black.
